chunks: And Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام:

That a man came to testify before Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, while his hand and foot had been amputated on the basis of testimony, so he accepted his testimony, and the man had repented and his repentance had become known.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam Ali عليه السلام in his authority and leadership
key_terms.شَهَادَتَهُ: his testimony in a legal setting
key_terms.شَهِدَ: gave testimony or appeared as a witness
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ: was amputated as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: Can the testimony of a person previously punished for a crime be accepted after repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that a person previously punished on the basis of testimony may have his testimony accepted after sincere tawbah is established and recognized. It reflects a legal principle in which known repentance restores credibility in judicial matters.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3308 - And it was narrated by Isma'il bin Muslim from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), from his father Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), peace be upon him,

that a man who had his hand and foot amputated based on testimony came to testify before Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. Imam (as) accepted his testimony, as the man had repented, and his repentance was known.
